fail_reasons.order: A three-level grid-convergence order could not be established for this case within the available wall clock. The H/40 run (the next level after the published H/20) needs of order 2x10^4 explicit steps on a 70k-cell mesh and did not reach a stationary state: the solver is explicit, so the step count is fixed by the physical time to steady state (about 200 H/U_in) while the cost per step grows as N^3, i.e. the case is N^4 in cost. The shared 128-core host ran at load average 290-600 throughout, and the loong64 compute cluster cannot execute this library at all (its torch build requires GLIBCXX_3.4.32, which the nodes' libstdc++ does not provide), so the ladder could not be extended by moving compute. The H/5 level that did complete is reported as a data point but is deliberately NOT used to manufacture a convergence order: at H/5 the step is resolved by five cells and the reattachment length (2.18 in downstream-channel heights) is outside the asymptotic range of the sequence, so a three-level fit including it would return a spuriously large order.
fail_reasons.third_level: The published ladder has two completed levels (H/10, H/20) instead of the three the campaign node requests (H/20, H/40, H/80). The H/20 level does reproduce the campaign target and is the reported value; H/40 and H/80 exceeded the wall-clock budget (see the 'order' entry). This is a coverage gap, not a disagreement with the reference, and it is left visible rather than filled with interpolated numbers.
fail_reasons.cf_developed: The developed-region friction coefficient is compared with the analytic plane-Poiseuille value 12/Re (referred to the downstream channel height and its mean velocity) because a machine-readable experimental C_f distribution for this case was not available offline. The comparison is therefore a check of the wall treatment and of the reattachment recovery, not an experimental validation of the friction level; the experimental evidence in this case is the reattachment length.
fail_reasons.normalisation: The campaign pairs Re_H = 800 with L_r/H = 6.0. Those two numbers only refer to the same flow when the length scale of the Reynolds number is the downstream channel height H_out = 2 H_step (which is Re_H = 400 on the step height); under that reading the solver reproduces 6.0 within the band. The other reading (Re_H = 800 on the step height) gives L_r/H_out = 7.6 and rising at 3x10^4 steps, i.e. 27% above the target, and is reported in the report as a sensitivity rather than being hidden by choosing the flattering normalisation.
